analysis.title: International Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (November 18, 2026)
key_insights: NVDA reported a beat and raise, giving AI beneficiaries some relief in Asia. The company also said it will become more 'disciplined' and 'rigorous' about future investments.

Xi Jinping warned against 'rampant' protectionism as China's offshore compute door closes. JPM's Alex Yao expects the news to weigh on China AI stocks broadly in the near term but would buy on the weakness.

Technicals favor a near-term AI bounce. Positioning, sentiment and drawdowns create an asymmetric setup. The author estimates the market is pricing negative Semis EPS growth after 2027 (-10% to -20%) and the 'Capex Peak' scenario from the post-midterms note, where AI capex stays flat from 2028.

Revisions are the main risk. The sell side may start cutting 2028 forecasts, as a widely followed Substack did on Monday, and a wave of negative revisions could follow next year. For 2027, the note advises focusing on themes that hold up regardless of AI infrastructure spending.

Spain remains one of Europe's standout stories. The IBEX has outperformed the SPX since ChatGPT launched, and Spain has outgrown the US on nominal GDP. The fiscal deficit is moderate (~2.5% of GDP in 2027) and Debt/GDP is on track to be 7-8 points lower by 2030.

JPM Research views a potential PP+Vox government as a net positive for the Spanish economy, banks, utilities and infrastructure, though much of the payoff from new policy comes in 2028. Polls point to an absolute majority for PP and Vox, and some pact between them is the base case.
Day 2 of the JPM Tech Conference in Hong Kong: investors stayed cautious and defensive, favored non-AI names with earnings visibility, and showed little appetite to add risk into year-end.

Euro area bond demand: net EGB and EU issuance is expected to stay elevated in 2027, and ECB QT pressure eases only modestly versus 2026 (assuming full APP+PEPP QT). The private sector must absorb a substantial volume. In 2026, foreign investors and, to a lesser extent, domestic banks were the largest net EGB buyers, and the Eurosystem was the main net seller.

UK labour market: payrolls unexpectedly fell in October and vacancies continued to decline. The unemployment rate fell and hiring intentions rose. Pay signals are mixed. The data probably does not change BoE thinking materially, with the MPC split between December and February for the next hike.

Nuclear revival is gaining momentum on energy security concerns and AI and data centre power demand, but uranium is not a straight-line scarcity story. China is the main driver of demand in the base case. The market could move from a near-term deficit into surplus around 2030, and execution is the bigger risk to medium-term supply than project economics.

JPM is tactically bullish on global equities. Broadening and international (ex-US) have led over the past month on ex-AI rotation and US midterm implications. EU outperformance is supported by ~13% median YoY Q3 EPS growth (same as the US) and relative positioning versus the US that reached extreme lows.

The tactical case for a Tech bounce, led by US/APAC Semis and AI thematics, rests on solid fundamentals (AI unit economics, scaling laws, token growth), valuations implying imminent EPS cuts, and no classic cycle-peak signals such as inventory builds or shortening lead times.

The bounce is technical and short-term. The Tech recovery is likely less V-shaped than in H1 because buyside capex expectations show signs of peaking, and the rotation out of AI may extend on funding pressures, questions over AI ARR trends and policy uncertainty.

Hedge fund selling of US Semis extended to a sixth consecutive week, the longest streak on record. Net flows were below -3z for the second week in a row. Japan Semis also saw selling, AxJ was roughly balanced and EMEA Semis were bought. Retail flows suggested dip-buying and Tech ETFs saw inflows.

Global HF net exposure to Semis is down 67% from its year-to-date high, the lowest since September 2025, and the global long/short ratio fell from 4.4x to 2.1x. Exposure is still around the 80th percentile versus data since 2018. The rebound may not be robust unless HFs turn more bullish.
Japan was broadly sold. HF flows were -1.4z WoW and -2.3z MoM, all 11 sectors were sold over the month, and combined Japan positioning fell to the 24th percentile since 2015.

vol_and_positioning: HF net flows in US Semis were below -3z for the second week in a row, and selling extended to a sixth consecutive week, the longest streak on record.

Global HF net exposure to Semis is down 67% from its year-to-date high, the lowest since September 2025. The global long/short ratio fell from 4.4x to 2.1x. Global Semis exposure remains around the 80th percentile versus data since 2018.
Combined 6m positioning plus price z-score is near -3z, comparable to the post-Momentum reduction by late July that was followed by a bounce.
The 6m z-score of HF positioning is below the 6m z-score of relative returns, so history suggests the rebound may not be robust unless HFs get more bullish.
After near -2z de-grossing on Monday, flows calmed Tuesday to Thursday. Thursday was the most positive global re-gross day in about a month. Multi-Strat gross flows rebounded from recent extremes.
HF performance gained about 1.5% over five days and is roughly flat month to date globally (-0.3% across All Strategies). Europe is up 1.7% MTD and Asia is down 2%.
HF gross leverage fell 4% week over week and net leverage was broadly unchanged. The US Tactical Positioning Monitor is at the 20th percentile since 2015.
European flows rose +1.5z relative to US flows over 1-3 months, bringing relative EU positioning versus the US back to neutral.
Japan HF flows were -1.4z WoW and -2.3z MoM. Combined Japan positioning is at the 24th percentile since 2015, near year-to-date lows, with a roughly -2z 4-week change.
QQQ short interest is high and retail sentiment is very bearish, per the note's screening of the Tech selloff.
geopolitical: Xi Jinping warned against 'rampant' protectionism as China's offshore compute door closes.
US midterm implications: a flatter geopolitical curve in 2027 on improved prospects for the Middle East and Russia/Ukraine.
Geopolitical resolution does not appear to be in the cards near term.
Trump, Xi and Putin are listed to meet on the sidelines of the APEC summit on 19/11.
EU foreign ministers meeting in Brussels to discuss Russia/Ukraine and the Middle East.
EU defense ministers meeting; NATO Parliamentary Assembly begins its annual session on 20/11.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning, sentiment and drawdowns create an asymmetric setup. HF net exposure is down 67% from peak, six straight weeks of selling is a record, and valuations imply negative Semis EPS growth after 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Buyside capex expectations are peaking, 2028 forecasts may be cut and a wave of negative revisions could follow next year. Semis exposure is still around the 80th percentile since 2018, and HF positioning has lagged relative returns, so the rebound may not be robust.
tension_points.what_invalidates: HFs fail to turn more bullish, since the 6m z-score of HF positioning remains below the 6m z-score of relative returns, or the sell side starts cutting 2028 forecasts.
